purpose: Machine-readable non-regression baseline for coordination hot paths.

items.title: Claim before deep context
items.observed_failure: Fresh workers spent minutes listing pins, G1/G2, heartbeats, returns and protocols before attempting authority.
items.invariant: Before first PIN/claim, a fresh /wc performs only bootstrap, beacon, one compact allocator read and bounded atomic claim attempts; only a proven-stale snapshot with two real CREATE_EXISTS collisions may trigger the single EFF034 compact-frontier refresh before the final attempt.

items.title: Surplus workers close cleanly
items.observed_failure: Workers with no assignment remained visible for minutes and could be mistaken for recoverable work.
items.invariant: No-PIN workers create no recovery debt and age out of Live's active list quickly.

items.title: Live publication cannot starve under commit bursts
items.observed_failure: cancel-in-progress caused repeated worker commits to cancel the feed publisher before it could publish.
items.invariant: The running Live publisher is never cancelled merely because a newer commit arrived; bursts coalesce through the pending run.

items.title: Only current authority appears active
items.observed_failure: Historical/superseded PIN generations inflated active/replacement counts.
items.invariant: Only the newest authoritative generation for a job is projected as its current owner; older generations remain history only.

items.title: Public /wc pointer cannot expand preclaim work
items.observed_failure: The public /wc pointer instructed workers to load Guide, Metabolism and page protocols before allocation, contradicting claim-first.
items.invariant: The public /wc pointer may route to canonical bootstrap and allocator but must not require unrelated deep protocols before ownership.

items.title: Prefer clean ready work and compiled roles over recovery archaeology
items.observed_failure: Workers entered expensive recovery validation while clean ready or centrally detectable Guide work was available.
items.invariant: Allocator and /wc rank clean execution first, then compiled role work, then recovery; stale recovery snapshots are never manually reconstructed preclaim.

items.title: Guide hydrates by relevance, not full-state ritual
items.observed_failure: Fresh /g required exhaustive queues/claims/runs/returns/heartbeats even when the request referenced one page, inbox item or bounded decision.
items.invariant: Guide loads identity + epoch + focus, resolves exact user referents, then expands only the relevant durable slice; raw global archaeology is fallback, not default.

items.title: Telemetry epoch cannot reset when ledger text changes
items.observed_failure: Using baseline file updated_at as telemetry activation would erase accumulated runtime samples whenever the ledger gained a new ratchet item.
items.invariant: Runtime measurement uses an explicit stable activation timestamp, independent from ordinary baseline edits.

items.title: Claim transport authorization must be explicit and fail fast
items.observed_failure: A fresh worker read one allocator but two claim CREATEs were blocked by tool authorization/safety controls, wasting most of a launch despite no job-level collision.
items.invariant: The canonical human invocation explicitly authorizes bounded reversible Prometeo writes; a transport-level claim block stops immediately and is never retried across multiple candidates.

items.title: Efficiency timing comes from durable repository events
items.observed_failure: A no-allocation receipt reused the launch timestamp even though the beacon and close commits were roughly 39 seconds apart, understating wasted time.
items.invariant: Runtime timing prefers Git commit time for beacon/claim/no-allocation persistence and treats model-authored timestamps as descriptive metadata, not the measurement clock.

items.title: Fast claim pins are complete before immutable create
items.observed_failure: A fresh /wc won an atomic G000001 with a minimal payload, then post-claim protocol loading revealed required immutable pin metadata was missing. Append-only pin semantics correctly forbade repairing that generation in place.
items.invariant: The compiled allocator supplies every mandatory portfolio pin field before CREATE; a fresh worker fills only bounded placeholders and never needs deep preclaim archaeology or post-create metadata repair.

items.title: Generation-fixed fixtures never enter ordinary next-generation recovery
items.observed_failure: A G000001-only contention fixture aged into replaceable state and the allocator offered G000002, producing ownership that could not satisfy the fixture contract.
items.invariant: Recovery generation semantics are machine-readable data. Fixed-generation work is excluded from ordinary G+1 recovery after its fixed generation exists, remains visible through a bounded attention route, and normal retry-safe work keeps G+1 recovery.

items.title: Latent useful work becomes claimable before NO_ALLOCATION
items.observed_failure: After claim-first removed worker archaeology, the fast allocator only exposed already-materialized jobs. Useful planning, integration, rescate and critic work remained latent even though Metabolism already had durable triggers, so fresh chats falsely ended NO_ALLOCATION while the project still had substantial work.
items.invariant: The central allocator compiles durable metabolism signals into deduplicated atomic role_ready candidates. Disposable workers never rediscover this state preclaim, and an empty concrete queue is not treated as project idleness while a grounded role trigger exists.

items.title: Explicit contention barriers precede the deterministic PIN race
items.observed_failure: A deliberate multi-worker PIN-race canary could publish a winner before another worker was durably armed, yielding winner-only evidence and forcing human timing or repeated canary launches.
items.invariant: Only jobs with explicit durable contention-barrier metadata receive a timing-only pre-PIN entrant/rendezvous action. Before valid RELEASE no portfolio PIN is attempted; timeout attempts no PIN; after RELEASE all entrants race the unchanged deterministic generation. Ordinary jobs remain direct-to-PIN.

items.title: Fingerprint churn cannot spawn concurrent GUIDE_RESCATE workers
items.observed_failure: While guide-rescate-98d380e06c22 had a fresh G000001 owner, the next allocator snapshot emitted guide-rescate-250858b98b36 because the LOW_YIELD evidence set changed. Fingerprint dedupe alone therefore allowed two concurrent rescate authorities for the same role and bottleneck class.
items.invariant: A fresh unreceipted GUIDE_RESCATE pin suppresses every other GUIDE_RESCATE role_ready candidate regardless of evidence fingerprint until that authority returns or becomes stale. Other Guide roles and ordinary execution remain claimable.

items.title: Historical transport blocks cannot create a permanent current regression
items.observed_failure: After the transport-authorization repair, five older CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED no-allocation events remained inside the stable runtime epoch. The efficiency snapshot counted the full epoch for its current alarm, so status stayed REGRESSION and kept spawning GUIDE_RESCATE even though the newest explicitly authorized worker acquired claims normally.
items.invariant: Historical transport-block incidents remain visible in cumulative telemetry, but the current CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED_REPEAT alarm is evaluated only over a bounded recent durable-event window. Ordinary ratchet edits never reset the global runtime epoch.

items.title: Explicit transport denials are telemetry, not GUIDE_RESCATE repair debt
items.observed_failure: Recent no-allocation pressure fed GUIDE_RESCATE directly. In the observed PROD-01 evidence, two of three recent receipts were explicit CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED safety/authorization denials, so an external non-repairable boundary could count toward repository self-repair and enter rescue evidence.
items.invariant: CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED remains visible in total no-allocation and transport-regression telemetry, but it does not count toward the recent-no-allocation GUIDE_RESCATE trigger and is excluded from repair evidence. Actionable no-allocation outcomes, generic-compatible recovery pressure, collisions and efficiency regressions preserve their rescue semantics.

items.title: role_ready evidence is validated centrally before claim
items.observed_failure: A compiled role_ready candidate can preserve either a nonexistent repo-local path or a syntactically existing file reference whose known semantic fragment does not resolve. Recovery compaction also previously dropped derived source_path and fabricated PORTFOLIO.json#job:<id> fallbacks for jobs that live only under derived/.
items.invariant: Every published role_ready candidate passes one central evidence-integrity stage: repo-local paths and recognized PORTFOLIO project/job fragments resolve before claim, derived recovery evidence preserves its durable source_path instead of fabricating seed anchors, invalid refs become machine-readable diagnostics and are removed from the claim payload or suppress an evidence-empty candidate, external annotated evidence remains valid, and role identity is not recomputed per worker.

items.title: Expired contention barriers stop consuming fresh workers after durable timeout evidence
items.observed_failure: A barrier deadline had already expired, yet the same dead fixture stayed at the front of ready and accumulated multiple per-worker timeout receipts. Fresh workers repeatedly spent a fast-allocation slot and append-only write proving the same timeout instead of reaching useful claimable work.
items.invariant: The first durable timeout receipt remains valid evidence that the barrier window expired without a PIN attempt. Once such evidence exists, the expired barrier candidate is removed from fast ready/recovery lanes, remains machine-readable in routing diagnostics/attention, and cannot demand another timeout write from each fresh worker.

items.title: Observability never becomes coordination overhead
items.observed_failure: Tracing can accidentally become another preclaim protocol, retry loop, authority dependency, or worker-repair swarm.
items.invariant: Wave observability is append-only, bounded to ROUTED/CLAIM_RESULT/CLOSE, best-effort, and strictly non-authoritative. Telemetry failure never blocks or changes allocation, ownership, execution, RETURN, recovery, or reallocation.

items.title: Capability-bound work is rejected before immutable ownership
items.observed_failure: Generic workers could claim specialized browser/network residuals and only discover after immutable PIN creation that the host could not satisfy the job, creating avoidable recovery generations and wasted ownership.
items.invariant: Durable required_capabilities flow into ready/recovery allocator candidates. A worker compares only allocator metadata with its already-known runtime/tool surface, skips before any PIN/claim/barrier write only when a requirement is definitively absent, treats unknown capability as compatible enough to attempt normal ownership, and never performs repository archaeology to prove capability fit.

items.title: Batched workers shard the unified compiled candidate mesh
items.observed_failure: Lane-local batching reduced some herd collisions, but hashing the raw unified mesh before runtime capability filtering still let multiple generic workers land inside different incompatible slots and then converge onto the same surviving Guide/recovery candidates. During WAVE-20260917-MESH-03-R1, two workers each exhausted three CREATE races after capability skips and collided on the same Guide/Guide/recovery pattern. The batch route must remain unified without allowing capability skips to collapse distinct shards.
items.invariant: When an explicit batch has n > 1 and the compact claim frontier publishes candidates, each worker first derives a stable local compatibility view from allocator-supplied required_capabilities using only definitely-known runtime absences, preserving published order and retaining unknown capabilities. The beacon SHA hash is applied to that filtered unified view, and collision rotation stays inside it. Batched workers do not re-impose lane priority locally; unbatched workers preserve ready -> queue_ready -> role_ready -> recovery. Atomic CREATE, bounded attempts and zero extra preclaim archaeology remain unchanged.

items.title: Guide signals survive Live compaction without publishing full histories
items.observed_failure: build-fast-allocator expected job.returns and job.collisions to derive RETURNS_UNCONSUMED, PARTIAL_LOOP and collision pressure, but build-live-feed deliberately stripped those arrays from feed.projects before publication. The compiler therefore lost the evidence cable and fell back disproportionately to generic recovery pressure.
items.invariant: Live exposes only bounded compact recent return/collision evidence needed by the allocator. The allocator consumes those compact refs, preserves PARTIAL/BOUNDARY attention after jobs age, and evaluates collision pressure only inside a bounded recent window. Full pin/claim/return/collision histories remain stripped from the public project projection.

items.title: Preclaim frontier remains compact and non-truncating
items.observed_failure: The full allocator first exceeded connector limits, then two PROD-01 workers still received a truncated supposedly-compact claim frontier at 24 candidates and closed without any authority attempt. A 64 KB target was therefore not transport-safe for the actual /wc runtime.
items.invariant: The ordinary hot path reads live/claim-frontier.json, a bounded compiler projection containing only exact claim data needed before ownership. The serialized frontier is hard-capped at 24,000 UTF-8 bytes; candidate count may shrink to preserve that transport invariant, while every published atomic CREATE payload remains exact. Full allocator.json remains diagnostic and forbidden on the ordinary preclaim path.

runtime_publication_observation.note: Published frontier is now byte-bounded; fresh-worker non-truncation still requires an authority attempt before RATCHETED.

items.title: Useful workers compound multiple productive units in one chat
items.observed_failure: Workers could still retire after a small fixed quota while a large compatible frontier remained, wasting already-open chat capacity and leaving long jobs unassisted.
items.invariant: Explicit-batch workers treat 3 productive units as a checkpoint, not a stop. They target 6 and may continue to 8 while compatible product/assist work remains. Safely decomposable long jobs may publish at most two non-overlapping assist children while the parent retains exclusive integration authority.

items.title: Branch-head churn does not impersonate an ownership collision
items.observed_failure: During WAVE-20260917-MESH-03, an unchanged beacon CREATE first received GitHub 409 because main moved from the connector's expected head, then succeeded on immediate retry. Another worker in the same batch spent its third authority slot on CAS_LOST after two genuine CREATE_EXISTS outcomes and closed NO_ALLOCATION. Branch-ref churn can therefore masquerade as a job collision and waste scarce claim attempts under concurrent commits.
items.invariant: Only exact target-path existence proves an ownership collision. An explicit branch-ref head mismatch gets one same-path, byte-identical CREATE stabilization retry with no pre-read and no authority-attempt cost; a second consecutive head movement stops as transport instability instead of consuming more candidate attempts.

items.title: Intentional SOURCE_DEBT does not self-spawn project planners
items.observed_failure: José STATE revision 8 explicitly recorded SOURCE_DEBT, an intentionally empty frontier, NEW_EVIDENCE_GATE and PLANNER_SPIN, yet the direct gap-only compiler emitted another PROJECT_FRONTIER_THIN candidate. EFF026 gated that compiler, but TKV1 then observed a freshly rebuilt 2026-09-18T15:24:46.054Z claim frontier still exposing guide-planner-project-jose-ee1004ddc96e with trigger PROJECT_COVERAGE_GAP: the downstream apply-project-coverage postprocessor was bypassing the same durable-state gate.
items.invariant: An intentional SOURCE_DEBT boundary with empty frontier_refs plus NEW_EVIDENCE_GATE must suppress both direct PROJECT_FRONTIER_THIN planning and downstream PROJECT_COVERAGE_GAP backfill. Every planner-producing compiler layer must consult the same durable project STATE gate. New evidence must change STATE to clear the predicate. Execution, integration, rescue and critic lanes remain unaffected.

items.title: Capability filtering precedes batched sharding
items.observed_failure: In WAVE-20260917-MESH-03-R1, generic workers with different beacon seeds skipped several specialized candidates after hashing because required capabilities were definitively absent, then converged on the same small set of role/recovery candidates and exhausted three authority attempts on CREATE_EXISTS.
items.invariant: For explicit batches, workers stable-filter only definitively incompatible candidates from the already-loaded compact frontier before applying the beacon hash. Surviving candidates retain compiler order, unknown capabilities remain eligible, no extra preclaim read/write is introduced, and atomic CREATE plus the three-attempt budget remain unchanged.

items.title: Historical no-allocation close tail cannot pin current regression
items.observed_failure: After WAVE-20260917-MESH-03-R1 exposed slow no-allocation closures, capability-filtered sharding was repaired. No newer NO_ALLOCATION event appeared after that repair, but live efficiency remained REGRESSION because NO_ALLOCATION_P90_GT_90S was computed from the full runtime epoch, so pre-repair 94/104/110-second closures kept re-materializing GUIDE_RESCATE work.
items.invariant: Historical no-allocation close latency remains visible in cumulative telemetry, while the current NO_ALLOCATION_P90_GT_90S alarm is evaluated only over a bounded recent durable-event window. The global runtime epoch is preserved and ordinary ratchet edits do not erase historical evidence.

items.title: Evidence-bound SOURCE_DEBT recovery requires a materially new basis
items.observed_failure: Jose V11 recovery reached a durable SOURCE_DEBT boundary, but elapsed-time replaceability alone emitted G3. Post-claim validation rejected G3 because no new artifact, evidence revision, capability or retry-safe trigger existed, wasting a worker generation while the unresolved job still needed to remain visible.
items.invariant: A completed nonterminal BOUNDARY/ROUTE_ABORTED that explicitly establishes SOURCE_DEBT is visible as recovery attention but does not emit another ordinary generation from age alone. Structured SOURCE_DEBT is compacted durably from same-job returns or one explicit bounded dependent return ref; OPEN exhaustive-negative debt suppresses time-only recovery even if later summaries omit SOURCE_DEBT, and malformed structured debt fails closed without fabricating completion. Recovery reopens only when a durable recovery_basis or newer explicitly referenced debt/source basis changes after the last return; the next PIN stamps both basis and dependency provenance. A worker that claims a new basis and then goes silent still uses ordinary stale-owner recovery. Fixed-generation policies and ordinary stale recovery remain unchanged.

items.title: Rolling pool replaces stop-start worker waves
items.observed_failure: Finite waves forced the human to wait for slow tail workers and repeatedly ask what to launch next, while useful capacity and frontier already existed. Raw worker count also obscured which execution pattern actually produced the most durable work.
items.invariant: POOL mode has no expected-count or cohort completion barrier. Workers use deterministic sharding, remain resident under existing stop laws, write one evidence-backed productivity exam at terminal close, and the rolling scoreboard compares useful output without rewarding verbosity. Growth evaluation occurs over rolling closed-worker windows and does not pause the pool absent a critical safety/authority regression.

items.title: Explicit claim denial is distinct from ambiguous transport
items.observed_failure: In WAVE-20260917-RESIDENCY-01, workers closed at 0-1 productive units after preclaim failures were durably collapsed into CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED. One receipt explicitly proved an authorization/safety denial, while another preserved no equally specific transport_result. Treating every unclassified write failure as an explicit denial discards capacity and hides whether the failure is policy, branch movement, path collision, or bounded transport ambiguity.
items.invariant: CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED is reserved for an explicit authorization/safety denial and stops immediately without retrying or bypassing the denied action. A pre-authority write failure that proves neither denial, target-path existence, nor branch-head movement is CLAIM_TRANSPORT_AMBIGUOUS and may divert at most once to one already-loaded untried compatible candidate with a different claim path. No extra preclaim read is allowed; a second ambiguous failure stops.

items.title: Authority-bound work requires new durable authority before recovery
items.observed_failure: Facultad canonical-identity discovery returned a nonterminal boundary requiring a new durable owner-authorized identity binding, but elapsed-time replaceability alone emitted G5 and then exposed G6 despite no new authority. Time was impersonating authorization and consuming workers.
items.invariant: AUTHORITY_DEBT / NEW_AUTHORITY_GATE is a structured durable gate distinct from SOURCE_DEBT and transport failure. OPEN or malformed authority gates remain visible as recovery attention but are not claimable by age. SATISFIED reopens only when a referenced durable evidence artifact exists and its satisfaction timestamp is later than the gate/boundary; the next PIN preserves authority-gate provenance. Jobs without an authority gate keep ordinary retry-safe recovery.

items.title: Fresh Guide inherits and writes back the active mission
items.observed_failure: A replacement /g could recover Prometeo identity and old succession material yet follow stale historical next_dot choreography, merely summarize context, or ask the human what to do next. That would lose the continuous-production objective and make transcript survival part of the control plane.
items.invariant: When CURRENT_MISSION_V1 is ACTIVE_BINDING, every fresh Guide loads it immediately after stable identity/EPOCH/Continuity Head, before stale historical next-step choreography. Bare /g executes safe useful mission work without an arbitrary one-action cap, persists material mission/campaign/project deltas or a Guide session receipt before replying, and never requires the human to reconstruct worker history. Stable entry, p.txt, Continuity Head and GRW001 expose the same mission pointer.

items.title: Proven-stale collision exhaustion gets one compact refresh
items.observed_failure: In PROD-01, workers could consume all three bounded CREATE attempts on paths already claimed from a compact frontier that had become stale, then close NO_ALLOCATION while fresh claimable work continued to appear. A snapshot may be fresh at first read yet age past 90 seconds during slow concurrent claim attempts; freezing the age decision at launch suppresses the bounded refresh after the two CREATE_EXISTS outcomes that prove collision pressure.
items.invariant: The ordinary hot path reads one compact frontier. After two real authority CREATE attempts return CREATE_EXISTS, if that already-loaded snapshot is older than 90 seconds at the post-collision refresh decision, the worker may reload exactly live/claim-frontier.json once, rebuild the same compatibility/sharding view, and spend only the remaining third authority attempt. Snapshot age is evaluated at that decision rather than frozen at first read. The exception adds no authority attempt, no broad archaeology, no transport bypass and no recovery authority.

items.title: Compatible frontier retention is contract-complete across bounded retries
items.observed_failure: A resident PROD-01 worker retained only candidate identities/claim paths after one compact frontier read. After its first CREATE_EXISTS, the next candidate's allocator-supplied claim_payload_shape was no longer available locally, so the worker stopped rather than reread the frontier or fabricate an immutable PIN payload.
items.invariant: The one compact frontier read remains sufficient for all bounded preclaim attempts because the local compatible candidate view retains each surviving allocator-published candidate object contract-completely. Display/log summaries never replace this retained object; collision/diversion advances use the retained claim payload with no reread or fabrication.

items.title: Human-decision project gates suppress fake frontier replenishment
items.observed_failure: calendar-habits reached VERIFIED_CANDIDATE_AWAITING_REVIEW with all mobile/touch criteria satisfied, an intentionally empty frontier, and an explicit HUMAN_DECISION_GATE. The project-guide scheduler only understood SOURCE_DEBT suppression, so frontier_min_per_project immediately emitted another PROJECT_FRONTIER_THIN planner that had no legitimate technical work to create. A concurrent valid integration then used the explicit status HUMAN_DECISION_GATE for the same semantic boundary, proving the suppression contract must recognize both canonical review-waiting forms rather than one literal status.
items.invariant: A project state explicitly waiting on Human disposition is a first-class nonterminal authority boundary, not a thin-frontier defect. When an allowlisted review-waiting status has empty frontier_refs and an explicit HUMAN_DECISION_GATE blocker, PROJECT_FRONTIER_THIN is suppressed without relabeling the state SOURCE_DEBT. A real frontier item, ACTIVE status, missing explicit gate, disabled policy, Human disposition, materially new candidate bytes, or durable contradictory defect evidence reopens normal planning.

items.title: Historical TTFA tail cannot pin current regression
items.observed_failure: After claim-first and compact-frontier repairs landed, current workers could acquire authority normally while live efficiency still stayed REGRESSION because TTFA_P90_GT_90S was computed from the full runtime epoch. Pre-repair 468-596 second authority delays therefore kept rematerializing GUIDE_RESCATE even though the hot path had already changed.
items.invariant: Historical time-to-first-authority latency remains visible in cumulative telemetry, while the current TTFA_P90_GT_90S alarm is evaluated only over a bounded recent durable authority-event window. The global runtime epoch is preserved and ordinary ratchet edits do not erase historical evidence.

items.title: High-yield leader triggers a bounded experiment, not status-only closure — historical YIELD-10X case
items.observed_failure: A fresh /g recovered the mission and found a 10/10 worker but only reported champion_reproducible=false and returned the human to external wake. It performed state correction but no multiplicative intervention to reproduce the observed high-yield pattern.
items.invariant: A high-yield leader must trigger a bounded measurable experiment rather than status-only Guide closure. The historical YIELD-10X-V1 experiment satisfied that intervention requirement but later failed independent reproduction and is now retired; it must remain immutable evidence, not an active worker assignment. EFF051 owns the current class-specific post-ownership experiment boundary.

items.title: Guide must provide strategic compass, creative multipliers and literal-response continuity
items.observed_failure: A fresh /g can execute correctly yet still feel mediocre by acting like an auditor: it reports status/gates and hands external wake back to the human without explaining whether the compounding plan is healthy, exploring multiplicative alternatives, preparing experiments/files, or preserving its exact visible answer for later quality critique.
items.invariant: After safe execution, a bare /g must orient the human as Guide. It updates the durable power compass, assesses parallelism/yield/reproduction/visible-value/autonomy, surfaces grounded multiplicative alternatives with minimal file/experiment plans, and persists the exact final visible response bytes before emitting them. Status-only handoff is insufficient when strategic analysis or multiplicative action is grounded.

items.title: Bare Guide ends with actionable utility footer and public brief
items.observed_failure: Even a strategically rich /g response can leave the human hunting for URLs, copying stale worker prompts, or asking which pages are online. Useful operational artifacts were scattered across prose and registries.
items.invariant: Every bare /g reply ends with a fixed utility footer containing the canonical Guide Brief link, Growth link, 1–8 directly relevant page URLs with short current context/status, the exact current /wc prompt in one copyable block, HUMAN ACTION or NONE, and the already-derived NEXT GUIDE CYCLE. The public Guide Brief is regenerated from Current Mission, Power Compass, project-guide states, page-watch registry and live worker views.

items.title: Fresh Guide quality takeover is phase-written and validator-enforced
items.observed_failure: A fresh Guide can technically load state and still skim instructions, stop after status narration, or claim success without proving ordered hydration, material action, strategic orientation, useful links and exact response persistence.
items.invariant: When the human message contains TAKEOVER CANARY TKV1, /g must execute the four durable phases 00_STARTED -> 10_HYDRATED -> 20_ACTED -> 30_FINAL. PASS requires ordered extracted-state proof, at least one material action, a substantive exact persisted response with strategic health, >=3 power levers, >=3 relevant direct page URLs, exact /wc prompt, Guide Brief/Growth, HUMAN ACTION and NEXT GUIDE CYCLE. CI validates the artifacts; missing phases or status-only action cannot PASS.

items.title: Guide growth trajectory makes compounding empirical and self-correcting
items.observed_failure: Even a competent Guide could solve local problems while gradually losing the human's real objective: continuously increasing useful work per chat, useful parallelism, visible product output and autonomy. The human had to notice drift manually because history, proof criteria and next branches were scattered.
items.invariant: Every bare /g loads the ACTIVE_BINDING empirical Growth Trajectory immediately after Current Mission, evaluates the active roadmap stage and drift alarms before local optimization, and updates the trajectory only on material evidence/stage changes. Cumulative counts never prove exponential growth. TRJ001 publicly exposes North Star, dated checkpoints, comparable-window proof gates, roadmap, action tree and anti-drift alarms. The Guide footer always links TRJ001 and explicitly distinguishes product progress from system/control-plane progress.

items.title: Frontier pressure is capability-aware
items.observed_failure: A clean frontier dominated by browser/mobile/host/dispatch-only work could satisfy the global frontier target numerically even when generic repository-capable /wc workers had little or no executable supply, hiding real FRONTIER_THIN pressure and sending generic capacity into collisions/recovery.
items.invariant: Allocator metabolism publishes total clean frontier separately from generic-compatible clean frontier and bounded specialized capability buckets derived only from candidate.required_capabilities. FRONTIER_THIN uses the generic-compatible count; specialized work remains visible and claimable to compatible workers; unknown capability remains unknown rather than being treated as absent or generic; claim authority, attempt bounds and POOL sharding are unchanged.

items.title: Capability-bound recovery does not masquerade as generic rescate pressure
items.observed_failure: LOW_YIELD rescue used the total replaceable recovery count. Browser/mobile/host-bound recovery could therefore cross the rescue threshold for generic repository-capable /wc workers, spawning mechanism-rescue work that could not supply the missing specialized runtime and amplifying low yield.
items.invariant: Allocator metabolism classifies recovery pressure from candidate.required_capabilities. Only generic-compatible recovery contributes to the replaceable-trigger arm of GUIDE_RESCATE LOW_YIELD. Specialized recovery remains visible and claimable to compatible workers and is published as bounded recovery_capability_pressure telemetry. Collision, efficiency-regression and recent-no-allocation rescue triggers remain unchanged.

items.title: Three-collision pool tail gets one retained-candidate rescue
items.observed_failure: In PROD-01, two recent workers each exhausted the ordinary three-authority-CREATE budget entirely on CREATE_EXISTS while their already-loaded compatible view still contained exactly one untried candidate. One receipt explicitly recorded untried_due_to_attempt_cap=[portfolio-recent-no-allocation-cause-mix-v1]; another recorded untried_compatible_due_to_attempt_cap=[guide-rescate-48ebd0d9d38e]. The three-attempt guard therefore converted proven stale/busy hints into avoidable NO_ALLOCATION even though one bounded, contract-complete candidate remained locally available.
items.invariant: The ordinary fast claim phase remains capped at three authority CREATE attempts. For BATCH/POOL only, after exactly three real candidate CREATE attempts all return CREATE_EXISTS, if the contract-complete compatible view still contains an untried candidate, the worker may spend exactly one POOL_TAIL_RESCUE CREATE on the next retained untried candidate. This exception performs no frontier reread, no lane reordering, no payload reconstruction, no directory archaeology and no authority bypass. Total authority CREATE attempts are hard-capped at four; any fourth collision or transport failure stops/re-enters allocation. Explicit denial, ambiguous transport, branch instability, capability mismatch, barrier timing and unbatched routing never unlock the tail rescue.

items.title: Specialized-only overload cannot starve the generic planner escape
items.observed_failure: Capability-aware frontier pressure correctly exposed generic-compatible clean work at zero while specialized work remained available, but overload_guard could still suppress the sole global FRONTIER_THIN planner. Generic PROD-01 workers then converged on a tiny compatible Guide/claim set and could exhaust collision budgets without creating generic executable supply.
items.invariant: The overload guard continues to suppress broad global planner replenishment whenever generic-compatible work exists. If and only if overload is active, generic-compatible clean frontier is exactly zero, specialized clean work exists, and grounded unresolved evidence exists, the existing deduplicated FRONTIER_THIN planner remains claimable as a bounded escape. Specialized work stays visible; authority, capability filtering, POOL sharding and filler prohibitions remain unchanged.

items.title: Already-owned Guide role paths never enter compact claim frontier
items.observed_failure: A stale compact claim frontier exposed two role_ready G000001 paths whose immutable Guide PIN files already existed, forcing fresh PROD-01 workers to burn two CREATE_EXISTS authority attempts before the bounded stale-refresh rule could help.
items.invariant: Before compact frontier publication, the existing Guide-pin suppression stage removes any role_ready candidate whose exact immutable claim_path is already materialized. Fresh role successors remain claimable, cross-fingerprint GUIDE_RESCATE suppression remains intact, specialized execution work is untouched, and workers gain no extra preclaim read.

items.title: GitHub Contents sha-missing 422 is a deterministic create-exists collision
items.observed_failure: Two PROD-01 workers received the same GitHub Contents atomic-CREATE response, HTTP 422 with message \"sha\" wasn't supplied. One correctly treated it as CREATE_EXISTS while another classified it CLAIM_TRANSPORT_AMBIGUOUS and stopped, wasting an otherwise healthy retained frontier.
items.invariant: For GitHub Contents atomic CREATE only, HTTP 422 whose normalized error contains the exact sha-missing update hint is deterministic target-path-exists evidence: classify CREATE_EXISTS and advance from the retained candidate view. Never broaden this into 'all 422 means collision'; other 422 responses retain evidence-based transport classification.

items.title: Recent NO_ALLOCATION cause mix stays bounded and evidence-backed
items.observed_failure: Recent NO_ALLOCATION closures were summarized as one low-yield signal, so transport truncation, exhausted claim races, explicit claim transport denial, ambiguous transport and capability exhaustion could not be distinguished without reopening worker history.
items.invariant: live/efficiency.json preserves cumulative NO_ALLOCATION telemetry and the exact bounded recent cause/receipt set. Efficiency-triggered LOW_YIELD Guide work receives the compact cause-summary ref plus exact actionable recent receipts; explicit CLAIM_TRANSPORT_BLOCKED receipts remain visible in telemetry but are excluded from repair evidence under EFF016B.

items.title: HTTP retrieval never impersonates a representative JavaScript browser
items.observed_failure: Repeated Jose V12 runtime-verification claims were won by workers that could search/fetch/navigate HTTP but had no tool capable of executing page JavaScript and interacting with the DOM, so post-claim validation repeatedly returned ROUTE_ABORTED instead of skipping the browser-only work before authority.
items.invariant: HTTP/search/fetch/navigation alone never satisfies representative_javascript_browser. When the runtime tool surface exposes retrieval/navigation but no JavaScript/DOM execution tool, representative_javascript_browser is definitively absent and the candidate is skipped with CAPABILITY_MISMATCH_PRECLAIM before any authority CREATE. Truly unresolved unrelated capabilities remain unknown rather than being treated as absent.

items.title: Post-ownership strategy experiments stay causally separated from claim authority
items.observed_failure: YIELD-10X-V1 was a post-ownership heuristic but its reproduction verdict was judged through a global score materially affected by preclaim collisions/no-allocation; after falsification, durable Guide state advanced to S3 while /wc and the exam still pointed at the retired universal candidate.
items.invariant: S3 strategy experiments load only after ownership, never alter claim-first, never newly propagate retired YIELD-10X-V1, record reconstructible class/variant evidence on v3.29 cards, use fresh class imbalance only after ownership with deterministic hash tie/fallback, compare post-ownership metrics within job class, publish preclaim waste only as separate diagnostics, and keep Growth Campaign operational rather than a competing strategy authority.

items.title: Mediated web access never impersonates unrestricted public-origin HTTP
items.observed_failure: STT and Tele public-origin verification jobs were repeatedly claimed by workers whose available web/search readers or code runtimes could not issue arbitrary DNS-resolved HTTP requests to the required origins. Post-claim execution then returned NETWORK_BOUNDARY/BOUNDARY, wasting durable ownership on a capability that the runtime contract could already prove absent.
items.invariant: Search/index retrieval, allowlisted or mediated web readers, repository fetchers, and general-purpose code runtimes explicitly without network never satisfy unrestricted_public_http_origin_fetch. If no runtime tool/primitive can issue arbitrary public-origin HTTP requests with DNS resolution to the candidate target class, the capability is definitively absent and the candidate is skipped with CAPABILITY_MISMATCH_PRECLAIM before authority. A genuine arbitrary HTTP client remains eligible; ambiguous or undocumented network capability remains unknown.

items.title: Evidence-bound SOURCE_DEBT silent-owner retries are bounded
items.observed_failure: The Jose V11 reviewable-preview chain had a durable exhaustive SOURCE_DEBT return requiring genuinely new byte-complete evidence, yet consecutive later owners could go silent. The SILENT_OWNER_STALE_AFTER_LAST_RETURN exception then kept reopening the unchanged stamped recovery basis, allowing G8/G9 and exposing G10 despite no new source or retry trigger.
items.invariant: Evidence-bound SOURCE_DEBT preserves one ordinary liveness retry after a silent post-return owner, but repeated silent owners on the same stamped recovery-basis fingerprint cannot reopen recovery indefinitely. Live state preserves the latest return generation; once two post-return generations exist without a newer return or changed basis, recovery is suppressed as SOURCE_DEBT_SILENT_OWNER_RETRY_EXHAUSTED and remains observable in recovery attention. New material basis evidence still re-enables recovery.

runtime_pending.observation: Long after G000010 became replaceable, the current allocator keeps the reviewable-preview job out of ordinary recovery and visible in recovery_attention. Its valid bounded SOURCE_DEBT dependency now wins over the malformed local derivative return, so the public allocator reports SOURCE_DEBT_BASIS_UNCHANGED rather than the earlier transient SOURCE_DEBT_MALFORMED_FAIL_CLOSED.
runtime_pending.truth_boundary: This runtime observation proves post-return fail-closed publication and valid dependency precedence. It does not prove that the exact SOURCE_DEBT_SILENT_OWNER_RETRY_EXHAUSTED branch fired after the repair, because no new stamped basis followed by two silent owners occurred.
runtime_pending.required_runtime_observation: Keep EFF053 pending for the exact repeated-silent same-basis branch unless a future natural runtime sequence exercises it. Do not manufacture silent owners merely to satisfy the metric.

items.title: Compact claim frontier preserves capability-signature diversity
items.observed_failure: The full allocator exposed public-HTTP-only recovery work, but the compact /wc frontier was filled by earlier browser-heavy rows and byte/candidate truncation hid every HTTP-only candidate. A worker with real unrestricted HTTP but no representative JavaScript browser could therefore appear idle even though compatible recovery existed.
items.invariant: The compact claim frontier preserves the allocator-preferred prefix and then promotes bounded first exemplars of previously unseen exact required_capabilities signatures before ordinary truncation. This does not change authority semantics or fabricate work; it only keeps distinct runtime-compatible lanes observable inside the bounded transport budget.

items.title: Launch-to-value growth pipeline measures every beacon without causal leakage
items.observed_failure: A 10-chat PROD-01 launch produced 10 durable beacons but only two explicit v3.28 terminal exams, while several workers collided, hit transport/capability boundaries or remained active. The strategy experiment therefore observed only survivors and product-value conversion was not measured separately from system/control work.
items.invariant: Every durable beacon receives a bounded derived launch measurement; explicit exams remain preferred and are the only source of strategy causal evidence. v3.29 balances A/B post-ownership from fresh explicit class counts with deterministic hash tie/fallback, carries allocator value_class and exact postclaim source hints, activates S4 capability specialization and S5 value dominance in parallel, soft-limits optional control overhead, and permits at most one grounded non-duplicate successor relay at terminal residuals.

items.title: Guide exhausts safe work before worker handoff and always gives an approximate launch count
items.observed_failure: The Guide could finish with a ready worker prompt while still having safe repository/CI/projection work available, and could withhold a launch count when runtime occupancy was stale. That pushed coordination back to the human even though frontier and measured funnel evidence were sufficient for a bounded approximate canary.
items.invariant: Before handing off to external /wc wake, the Guide must continue grounded reversible same-turn work until no material internal action remains or a true human/authority/privacy/capability boundary is reached. The first visible copyable block is the exact canonical Current Mission worker prompt. The final mini line gives an evidence-based approximate number of identical /wc launches before returning to /g. Stale runtime forbids fake exactness but never permits count-withholding when a bounded frontier/sample estimate is possible. Human worker routing remains forbidden.

items.title: Fresh /wc launch identity cannot replay a historical terminal worker
items.observed_failure: A newly opened canonical /wc chat answered with the exact historical completion for wc-20260918T212321Z-94fec87501 (v3.28, closed the previous day) and created no new current worker beacon. The content was historically true but was replayed as if it were current execution.
items.invariant: Every new human /wc invocation generates a de-novo current-turn worker_id and launch_nonce, atomically creates its own beacon before allocation, and may not emit a terminal response unless that beacon exists. Historical worker ids/exams/returns/no-allocation/CLOSE records can never substitute for the current launch. v3.30 exams bind launch_nonce to the beacon. A CREATE_EXISTS beacon identity is discarded and regenerated, never adopted.

items.title: Canonical /wc human prompt is a self-guarding fresh resident launch envelope
items.observed_failure: Repository/public bootstrap v3.30 already contained an anti-replay rule, but a newly opened chat could answer from historical project/model context before dereferencing /wc. That let a true old completion masquerade as the current launch. Separately, POOL residency depth was more explicit in internal protocol than in the human launch envelope.
items.invariant: The exact canonical human /wc prompt itself declares a NEW worker, requires this turn's own fresh beacon as the first durable action, forbids historical identity/result substitution, and states POOL residency depth (3 checkpoint, target 6, cap 8 except a real boundary). The public /wc launcher is generated from Current Mission so prompt text cannot silently drift. Below-target exhaustion must be proven from this launch's post-RETURN fresh compact frontier, never inherited from historical no-allocation evidence.

items.title: Malformed local SOURCE_DEBT cannot mask a valid bounded dependency
items.observed_failure: After the Jose V11 G000010 control-plane return, Live projected a latest same-job source_debt object that was intentionally derivative and lacked the standalone exhaustive-search fields. structuredSourceDebtState preferred that invalid local projection over the job's independently valid exact bounded source_debt_dependency, so the compact frontier suppressed the job as SOURCE_DEBT_MALFORMED_FAIL_CLOSED instead of preserving the causal unchanged dependency semantics.
items.invariant: A malformed/derivative latest local SOURCE_DEBT record must still fail closed when it is the only debt evidence. But when the job carries an independently valid explicit bounded source_debt_dependency, that dependency remains the authoritative structured debt state and cannot be masked by the invalid local projection. The fallback is limited to the already-projected exact dependency and never recursively traverses return evidence.

items.title: POOL residency is measurable and unjustified early terminals cannot pass fresh-launch smoke
items.observed_failure: v3.30 declared checkpoint 3, target 6 and hard cap 8, but the fresh-launch smoke could pass from beacon/nonce integrity alone even if a pooled worker explicitly closed below target without durable evidence of a real boundary or compatible-frontier exhaustion.
items.invariant: For v3.30 POOL launches, active or derived workers are not residency failures. An explicit terminal exam below 6 durable productive units must name an allowed real close_reason and at least one durable close_evidence_ref; otherwise the launch is EARLY_CLOSE_UNJUSTIFIED and cannot count as one of the three conforming fresh workers required for smoke PASS.

items.title: Compact claim frontier preserves bounded zero-capability capacity under specialization pressure
items.observed_failure: The live allocator exposed multiple no-special-capability claims/recoveries while the 24KB compact claim frontier collapsed required_capabilities=[] to a single capability signature. Under a specialized-heavy frontier, generic /wc workers could therefore see only one or two compatible claim paths and collide/close even though additional compatible durable work existed.
items.invariant: Capability-signature diversity remains preserved, but the compact frontier also protects a bounded minimum of four distinct candidates whose required_capabilities array is empty when that many exist. This is transport ordering only: allocator prefix, 24KB cap, claim payloads and atomic authority semantics remain unchanged.
